en.t: Having said that, I reflected again and asked myself:

units.source_text: 为什么喜欢引起别人的猜疑卿对我自己来说，这是没有什么疑问的，是明摆着的事。

en.t: Why did I like to arouse other people's suspicion? To me, there was no doubt about it; it was perfectly obvious.

units.source_text: 我的感情也会像口吃一样打顿。

en.t: My feelings, too, would falter like a stutter.

units.source_text: 我的感情总是赶不上趟。

en.t: My feelings were always late in catching up.

units.source_text: 其结果，父亲的死这件事，同悲伤这种感情是彼此孤立的，互不相联系，也互不相侵犯的。

en.t: As a result, the event of my father's death and the feeling called sorrow stood isolated from each other, neither connected nor encroaching on one another.

units.source_text: 往往由于时间上差错一点或是晚了一点，我的感情和事件就会完全被拉回到七零八落的状态。

en.t: Often, because of the slightest mismatch in timing or a small delay, my feelings and the event would be pulled completely back into a scattered, disjointed state.

units.source_text: 大概它的本质就是七零八落的吧。

en.t: Perhaps its very nature was to be scattered and disjointed.

units.source_text: 如果说我有自己的悲伤，那么它同任何事件、任何动机都毫不相干，是突然的，毫无道理地向我袭来的……

en.t: If I had a sorrow of my own, then it had nothing at all to do with any event or motive; it came upon me suddenly, without the least reason...
